source.author: verg
source.text: Tum Cererem corruptam undis Cerealiaque arma expediunt fessi rerum, frugesque receptas et torrere parant flammis et frangere saxo.
source.text_original: Tum Cererem corruptam undis Cerealiaque arma / expediunt fessi rerum, frugesque receptas / et torrere parant flammis et frangere saxo.
source.text_english: Then, wearied by their plight, they recover the grain-damaged Ceres and her Cerial implements, and they prepare the rescued crops both to parch them in the flames and to crush them with stone.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Objiciunt mihi sectatores ejus, cerealiaque arma Expediunt fessi rerum, quare libros Origenis noxios, et Ecclesiasticae fidei repugnantes, in Latinum sermonem verterim.
reuse.text_original: Objiciunt mihi sectatores ejus, cerealiaque arma Expediunt fessi rerum, quare περὶ Ἀρχῶν libros Origenis noxios, et Ecclesiasticae fidei repugnantes, in Latinum sermonem verterim.
reuse.text_english: His followers throw this at me, and, wearied by the situation, they take up “cerealian” weapons: why, they ask, did I translate into Latin books of Origen that are harmful and contrary to the faith of the Church?
